verify_first.label: Resolve this before anything else
verify_first.body: Still the SIC-combination question — whether Endeavor's asterisk rule lets your military SIC time count toward PIC / PIC Cross Country / PIC Night. If yes, PIC+qualifying-SIC sits at 385.9/250 (154%), well clear. If no, strict PIC is the number that matters, and it's climbing fast on its own: 84.6/250 (34%) now, up from 49.5 two weeks ago — every dual instrument lesson adds PIC since you're rated (FAR 61.51(e)). Confirm the rule with your recruiter, but this is no longer a blocker either way.

stalled.label: Stalled — needs a deliberate decision
stalled.body: Multi-Engine Land: 13.8/25 (55%), unchanged since your last DA-42 session in June 2025. Nothing in instrument or commercial single-engine training touches this — it will not self-resolve. Still needs dedicated multi-engine time booked specifically.

resolving_naturally.label: Resolving on its own — don't force it
resolving_naturally.body: You're deep in instrument checkride prep now (mock checkride 8/17, three prep flights through 8/20) — the instrument rating is essentially in hand. Instrument time (43.2/75, 58%) and Cross Country (367.5/500, already well past the 200-hr Restricted-ATP floor) keep climbing through the syllabus. Strict PIC and PIC Cross Country ride along the same way (both grow whenever you fly a dual lesson as sole manipulator) — PIC XC is now 51.5/100 (52%), over half way — so don't chase them separately.

highest_leverage.label: Highest-leverage move for total hours
highest_leverage.body: Pace has accelerated hard: 35.1 hrs in the 15 days since the last review (~70 hrs/month, vs. ~36 last month) — at this rate 750 total time is roughly 2.8 months out. That's checkride-season intensity and won't hold year-round, but it shows the trajectory. Once the instrument checkride is done, Commercial → CFI remains the fastest sustainable path: instructing builds PIC and total hours faster than paying for rentals, and closes the strict-PIC gap directly.

lagging.label: Lagging without a natural fix
lagging.body: PIC Night: 1.6/25 (6%) — still the clear laggard, untouched by all the recent flying. Night overall is 48.0/100 (48%), but none of the post-checkride flights combined PIC and night on the same leg. This is the one category worth deliberately scheduling around: a few dedicated night instrument or night XC legs now count as PIC night automatically, and nothing in the normal syllabus forces them.
